Graceful shutdown middleware. Handles SIGTERM/SIGINT, drains in-flight requests, and runs cleanup hooks.

Signal delivery is async-signal-safe: the handler only sets a volatile flag. On POSIX a dedicated drain thread (10ms flag poll, off the async event loop) performs shutdown initiation + drain checks, so the event loop never polls and signal-to-shutdown latency is bounded by 10ms. A self-pipe was avoided because re-declaring C write/read conflicts with unistd.h signatures. Shutdown hooks run exactly once when the drain completes, either on the drain thread or on the thread whose last in-flight request finished (whichever observes the completion first), and always before any forced exit.

Concurrency model (important): the drain thread only touches state objects through a lock-free registry of raw pointers. Objects stay alive because registration pins them with GC_ref and the main thread releases the pin (after drain + hooks finished and after a drain-thread quiescence point) in cleanupFinishedDrainStates, which the middleware runs at creation. The drain thread never creates threads, never frees GC memory, and never allocates in its steady-state loop (all log output uses literal strings).

Note: installing the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers REPLACES any handlers the application previously registered for those signals (they are not chained, because a signal handler must stay gcsafe/raises: [] and cannot invoke an arbitrary prior handler). Pass installSignalHandlers = false to opt out.
